The memorial honors the more than 5,000 slaves and free Black persons who fought for independence in the American Revolution. An earlier act, Public Law 112-239, let the National Mall Liberty Fund D. C. build it on federal land. The General Services head told Congress the site should be in Area I. The resolution then approves that site.
plaw-113-177-2014: A hydroelectric license at American Falls Reservoir is revived by Public Law 113-177 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The project is Federal Energy Regulatory Commission project number 12423. The Federal Power Act sets a start span that would otherwise apply. At the license holder's request, and after fair notice, the Commission must act. It must bring the license back in force. It must also stretch the span to start building to three years from the date this act passed.
plaw-113-178-2014: A canal park panel gains a longer life under Public Law 113-178 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The panel is the Chesapeake and Ohio Canal National Historical Park Commission. It works under section 6 of the Chesapeake and Ohio Canal Development Act. The act states one change to that scheme. The Commission now ends 10 years after the date this act passed. No other term of the panel's work is set out in the text.
plaw-113-179-2014: Public Law 113-179, the Gun Lake Trust Land Reaffirmation Act, locks in a land trust for a Michigan tribe. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014. The land was taken into trust for the Match-E-Be-Nash-She-Wish Band of Pottawatomi Indians. An Interior Department notice of May 13, 2005, describes the ground. The act affirms the land as trust land. It also ratifies the acts of the Interior Secretary in taking it. Suits on the land may not be filed or kept in federal court.
plaw-113-180-2014: A children's emergency care program is renewed by Public Law 113-180 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. Its short title is the Emergency Medical Services for Children Reauthorization Act of 2014. It amends section 1910 of the Public Health Service Act. The old text set one sum, $30,387,656, after the word and. The act strikes that and, keeping the same sum. It then adds $20,213,000 for each of fiscal years 2015 through 2019.
plaw-113-181-2014: Pay rates for hurt veterans rise under Public Law 113-181, the Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2014. The 113th Congress passed it in September 2014. From December 1, 2014, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs must raise the sums in effect on November 30, 2014. The raise covers disability pay for veterans with service-linked harm. It also covers dependency and indemnity pay for survivors of some disabled veterans. The list of sums starts with wartime disability pay.
plaw-113-182-2014: Public Law 113-182, the Debbie Smith Reauthorization Act of 2014, renews DNA backlog programs. The 113th Congress amended the DNA Analysis Backlog Elimination Act of 2000. Year spans shift across three sections. In one place, 2010 through 2018 becomes 2014 through 2019. In two more places, 2009 through 2014 becomes 2015 through 2019. A second act gains the same new span. It covers training and teaching, and grants for sexual assault forensic exams.
plaw-113-183-2014:
Public Law 113-183, the Preventing Sex Trafficking and Strengthening Families Act, was passed by the 113th Congress in 2014. Its stated aims are three. It seeks to stop sex trafficking of children in foster care. It extends and improves adoption incentives. It also improves child support recovery across borders.

Title I is called Protecting Children and Youth at Risk of Sex Trafficking. Subtitle A covers finding and shielding such children. Its sections require states to mark at-risk youth, record their cases, and set services for them. Reports of trafficking are required. Trafficking data must enter the foster care data system.
plaw-113-184-2014: Public Law 113-184 is a joint resolution of the 113th Congress, approved on September 29, 2014. It fills one seat on the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution. The seat is in the class of members who are not in Congress. France A. Cordova of Indiana left it by resignation on March 13, 2014. Michael Lynton of California takes the seat. His term runs 6 years from the date the resolution passed.
plaw-113-185-2014:
Shared assessment data for post-acute care is the goal of Public Law 113-185 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. People know it as the IMPACT Act of 2014. It amends title XVIII of the Social Security Act. The goal is shared assessment data for post-acute care. Post-acute care is care given after a hospital stay, in a rehab or nursing setting.

A new section 1899B sets the rule. The Secretary must require post-acute care providers to report shared patient assessment data. Reports also cover quality measures. The data serves quality checks, payment calls, and discharge planning. That shared base lets unlike care sites be judged on one scale.
plaw-113-186-2014:
Public Law 113-186, the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 2014, renews and improves the 1990 act of the same short name. The 113th Congress passed it in November 2014. Section 2 rewrites the purposes of the older act. The first purpose is room to move. Each state gets the most freedom that can be had in shaping child care programs for its own children and parents.

A second purpose is parental choice. Working parents gain power to pick the care that best fits their family. A third purpose is buyer facts for parents. States are urged to give facts that help parents make sound choices on care. The purposes list goes on past the sample's end.
plaw-113-187-2014:
Public Law 113-187, the Presidential and Federal Records Act Amendments of 2014, updates how federal records are kept. The 113th Congress amended chapter 22 of title 44. That chapter is known as the Presidential Records Act. The act sets steps for weighing claims of privilege, based in the Constitution, against release of presidential records.

The contents list shows the act's reach. Sections cover presidential records and the National Archives body. Others cover records work by federal agencies and disposal of records. One section sets steps to stop wrongful removal of classified records from the Archives.
plaw-113-188-2014:
Public Law 113-188, the Government Reports Elimination Act of 2014, cuts federal reporting duties. The 113th Congress passed it to end or change reports that agencies owe. The act is sorted by department, one title at a time. Title I covers the Department of Agriculture and is headed Reports eliminated. Title II does the same for the Department of Commerce.

Title III covers the Corporation for National and Community Service. Title IV covers the Department of Defense. Title V covers the Department of Education, with one named Impact Aid report. Title VI covers the Department of Energy, where the sample ends.
plaw-113-189-2014: Danville, Vermont, gains a named post office under Public Law 113-189 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 35 Park Street in Danville must be known as the Thaddeus Stevens Post Office. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name. The act does nothing else.
plaw-113-190-2014: The short title Albuquerque, New Mexico, Federal Land Conveyance Act of 2013 belongs to Public Law 113-190 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. It lets the head of General Services convey one parcel in Albuquerque. The buyer is the Amy Biehl High School Foundation. The land sits at 123 Fourth Street, SW, by the Old Post Office building. Its lots are numbered 12 through 19, as the survey finds them. The townsite is the New Mexico Town Company's Original Townsite.
plaw-113-191-2014: Hazlehurst, Mississippi, gains a named post office building under Public Law 113-191 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 130 Caldwell Drive in Hazlehurst must be known as the First Lieutenant Alvin Chester Cockrell, Jr. Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name. The act does nothing else.
plaw-113-192-2014: Public Law 113-192, passed in 2014 by the 113th Congress, names one post office in Nebraska. The Postal Service site at 278 Main Street in Chadron must be known as the Sergeant Cory Mracek Memorial Post Office. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name.
plaw-113-193-2014: Rochester, New York, gains a named post office under Public Law 113-193 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 1335 Jefferson Road in Rochester must be known as the Specialist Theodore Matthew Glende Post Office. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name. The act does nothing else.
plaw-113-194-2014: Public Law 113-194, the Clifford P. Hansen Federal Courthouse Conveyance Act, moves a Wyoming courthouse to a county. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014. The courthouse is the land and building at 145 East Simpson Street in Jackson, Wyoming. The head of General Services must offer to convey all federal rights in it to Teton County. A payment part then begins, in which the county gives value in exchange. The sample ends in the middle of that part.
plaw-113-195-2014: Public Law 113-195, the Sunscreen Innovation Act, sets a new review path for sunscreen drugs sold without a prescription. The 113th Congress amended the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act in 2014. The new path judges the safety and strength of active ingredients in such sunscreens. A new subchapter holds the rules, starting with section 586. One term is the final sunscreen order. That order states that an ingredient is GRASE, or broadly known as safe and sound for its use.
plaw-113-196-2014: Public Law 113-196, the Traumatic Brain Injury Reauthorization Act of 2014, renews brain injury programs in the Public Health Service Act. The 113th Congress passed it in November 2014. It covers work by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on prevention and tracking of such harm. One edit updates a health goals cite. The words Healthy People 2010 become Healthy People 2020. A second part rewrites the funds section, numbered 394A, as the sample breaks off.
plaw-113-197-2014: Screen labels for licensed devices are promoted by Public Law 113-197 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. Its short title is the Enhance Labeling, Accessing, and Branding of Electronic Licenses Act, or E-LABEL Act. The act backs non-exclusive use of electronic labeling for devices licensed by the Federal Communications Commission. Findings say the Commission first set standard physical labels in 1973. As devices shrink, those labels grow harder and costlier to fit. Many makers and buyers would rather show the facts on the device screen.
plaw-113-198-2014: A Medicare enforcement pause for small hospitals is extended through 2014 by Public Law 113-198 of the 113th Congress. The pause covers supervision rules for outpatient therapeutic services. The hospitals in scope are critical access hospitals and small rural hospitals. The Health and Human Services Secretary must keep applying an enforcement note from November 1, 2012. That note gave the hospitals a break from a restated direct supervision rule. Direct supervision means a doctor must be on hand while care is given.
plaw-113-199-2014: The federal charter of the Veterans of Foreign Wars is updated by Public Law 113-199 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The change reflects the service of women in the armed forces. Section 230101 of title 36 had used the word men for the group. The act strikes men and inserts veterans. A purposes clause had used the word widows. The act strikes widows and inserts surviving spouses. Those two swaps are the whole act.
plaw-113-200-2014:
Public Law 113-200, the STELA Reauthorization Act of 2014, extends rules on the relay of television broadcast signals. The 113th Congress amended the Communications Act of 1934 and title 17. Title I holds the communications parts. Section 101 extends the power in scope. Section 102 reshapes television markets so viewers can reach programs that fit their area.

Later sections guard buyers in retransmission consent deals. One delays a joint sales rule, and one repeals the integration ban. Reports fill the rest of the title. They cover market areas, cable rates, and local network channel broadcasts. Section 2 states that no added funds are granted by the act.
plaw-113-201-2014: Public Law 113-201 is a joint resolution of the 113th Congress, approved on December 4, 2014. It does one thing only. It appoints the day the One Hundred Fourteenth Congress first meets. That first regular session must begin at noon on Tuesday, January 6, 2015. The House passed the resolution on November 14, 2014. The Senate passed it on November 20, 2014.
plaw-113-202-2014: Public Law 113-202 is a joint resolution of the 113th Congress, approved on December 12, 2014. It makes further continuing appropriations for fiscal year 2015. The resolution amends the Continuing Appropriations Resolution, 2015, which is Public Law 113-164. It strikes the date in section 106 and inserts December 13, 2014. That one-day move kept the stopgap funding in force. Both chambers passed it on December 11, 2014.
plaw-113-203-2014: Public Law 113-203 is a joint resolution of the 113th Congress, approved on December 13, 2014. It makes further continuing appropriations for fiscal year 2015. The resolution amends the Continuing Appropriations Resolution, 2015, which is Public Law 113-164. It strikes the date in section 106 and inserts December 17, 2014. The swap added four days to the stopgap funding. The House passed it on December 12 and the Senate a day later.
plaw-113-204-2014: Cold Spring, Minnesota, gains a named memorial post office under Public Law 113-204 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 14 Red River Avenue North in Cold Spring must be known as the Officer Tommy Decker Memorial Post Office. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name. The act does nothing else.
plaw-113-205-2014: Houston, Texas, gains a named post office building under Public Law 113-205 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 4110 Almeda Road in Houston must be known as the George Thomas 'Mickey' Leland Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name. The act does nothing else.
plaw-113-206-2014: Public Law 113-206, passed in 2014 by the 113th Congress, names one post office in Florida. The Postal Service site at 500 North Brevard Avenue in Cocoa Beach must be known as the Richard K. Salick Post Office. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name.
plaw-113-207-2014: London, Ohio, gains a named memorial post office under Public Law 113-207 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 25 South Oak Street in London must be known as the London Fallen Veterans Memorial Post Office. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name. The act does nothing else.
plaw-113-208-2014: Champaign, Illinois, gains a named post office building under Public Law 113-208 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 302 East Green Street in Champaign must be known as the James R. Burgess Jr. Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name. The act does nothing else.
plaw-113-209-2014: Monroe, New York, gains a post office with a long memorial name under Public Law 113-209 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 787 State Route 17M in Monroe must carry a long name. It is the National Clandestine Service of the Central Intelligence Agency NCS Officer Gregg David Wenzel Memorial Post Office. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the full name.
plaw-113-210-2014:
Jack Nicklaus receives a gold medal under Public Law 113-210 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The medal honors his service to the nation in promoting excellence, good sportsmanship, and giving. Section 1 calls him a world-famous golf professional and a keen giver. It also calls him a business leader and a devoted husband, father, and grandfather.

The findings count 120 wins in top-level professional play. Of those, 73 came on the PGA Tour. His 18 major titles still set the mark for all golfers. He won the first at the 1962 U. S. Open, at age 22.
plaw-113-211-2014: Munising, Michigan, gains a named post office building under Public Law 113-211 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 220 Elm Avenue in Munising must be known as the Elizabeth L. Kinnunen Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name. The act does nothing else.
plaw-113-212-2014:
Coins for the centennial of World War I are ordered by Public Law 113-212 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. Its short title is the World War I American Veterans Centennial Commemorative Coin Act. The Treasury Secretary must mint the coins. Section 2 gives the facts. The year 2018 marks 100 years since the armistice with Germany ended the fighting.

The United States entered the war on April 6, 1917, by declaring war on Germany. Two million American soldiers served overseas. More than four million men and women served in uniform in all. Over 9 million soldiers worldwide lost their lives between 1914 and 1918.
plaw-113-213-2014: Miami, Florida, gains a named post office building under Public Law 113-213 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 10360 Southwest 186th Street in Miami must be known as the Larcenia J. Bullard Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name. The act does nothing else.
plaw-113-214-2014: Public Law 113-214, passed in 2014 by the 113th Congress, names one post office building in Illinois. The Postal Service site at 3349 West 111th Street in Chicago must be known as the Captain Herbert Johnson Memorial Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name.
plaw-113-215-2014: A veterans clinic to be built in Colorado Springs, Colorado, is named by Public Law 113-215 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The community-based outpatient clinic of the Department of Veterans Affairs will stand at 3141 Centennial Boulevard in Colorado Springs. It must be known as the PFC Floyd K. Lindstrom Department of Veterans Affairs Clinic. Any mention of that building in a federal law, rule, map, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the full name.
plaw-113-216-2014: Jackson, Michigan, gains a named memorial post office under Public Law 113-216 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 113 West Michigan Avenue in Jackson must be known as the Officer James Bonneau Memorial Post Office. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name. The act does nothing else.
plaw-113-217-2014: Mankato, Minnesota, gains a named veterans clinic under Public Law 113-217 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The community based outpatient clinic of the Department of Veterans Affairs stands at 1961 Premier Drive in Mankato. It must be known as the Lyle C. Pearson Community Based Outpatient Clinic. Any mention of that clinic in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the full name.
plaw-113-218-2014: Springfield Gardens, New York, gains a named post office building under Public Law 113-218 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 218-10 Merrick Boulevard in Springfield Gardens must be known as the Cynthia Jenkins Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name. The act does nothing else.
plaw-113-219-2014: Hilliard, Ohio, gains a post office building with a joint memorial name under Public Law 113-219 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 4000 Leap Road in Hilliard must carry a joint name. It is the Master Sergeant Shawn T. Hannon, Master Sergeant Jeffrey J. Rieck and Veterans Memorial Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the full name.
plaw-113-220-2014: A Vermilyea Avenue site in New York City is named by Public Law 113-220 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 90 Vermilyea Avenue in New York, New York, must be known as the Corporal Juan Mariel Alcantara Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name. The act does nothing else.
plaw-113-221-2014: Public Law 113-221, the Honor Flight Act, speeds airport screening for veterans on honor trips. The 113th Congress amended title 49 in 2014. The head of the Transportation Security Administration must set up a process with the Honor Flight Network, or a like nonprofit group. The process gives fast and dignified screening to veterans on a private charter flight. Their trip takes them to war memorials built to honor their service. A new section 44928 holds the rule.
plaw-113-222-2014: Public Law 113-222, passed in 2014 by the 113th Congress, names one post office in Ohio. The Postal Service site at 715 Shawan Falls Drive in Dublin must be known as the Lance Corporal Wesley G. Davids and Captain Nicholas J. Rozanski Memorial Post Office. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the full name.
plaw-113-223-2014:
Public Law 113-223, the Bill Williams River Water Rights Settlement Act of 2014, settles water claims in Arizona. The 113th Congress told the Interior Secretary to enter two deals. One is the Big Sandy River-Planet Ranch Water Rights Settlement Agreement. The other is the Hualapai Tribe Bill Williams River Water Rights Settlement Agreement. Land at Planet Ranch, on the Bill Williams River, is leased under the plan.

The lease serves the Lower Colorado River Multi-Species Conservation Program. Section 2 states the aims. The deal must be a fair and final settlement of claims to water in the river watershed. The Hualapai Tribe is one party named. The Interior Department, acting for itself and others, is the next party named.
plaw-113-224-2014: Simi Valley, California, gains a named post office under Public Law 113-224 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 2551 Galena Avenue in Simi Valley must be known as the Neil Havens Post Office. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name. The act does nothing else.
plaw-113-225-2014: Princeton, Florida, gains a named post office building under Public Law 113-225 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The building stands at 13500 SW 250 Street. Its new legal name is the Corporal Christian A. Guzman Rivera Post Office Building. In maps, rules, and files of the United States, a mention of the site is read as a mention of that name.
plaw-113-226-2014: Vallejo, California, gains a named post office building under Public Law 113-226 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. Head to 100 Admiral Callaghan Lane and you reach the site in question. Congress directs that it be called the Philmore Graham Post Office Building. Older papers that name the site count, in law, as naming it by the new title.
plaw-113-227-2014: A law school clinic program at the patent office is set up by Public Law 113-227 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The program sits in the United States Patent and Trademark Office. Students in a member law school's clinic may practice patent and trademark law before the Office. They draft, file, and press claims for clients who qualify for clinic aid, at no charge. The Director must set the rules for joining. All law schools with American Bar Association approval may take part.
plaw-113-228-2014: A change to an atomic energy pact with the United Kingdom is approved by Public Law 113-228 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The pact joins the United States and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland. It covers work with atomic energy for mutual defense. The changes were made at Washington on July 22, 2014. They were sent to Congress on July 24, 2014. The act approves them in full. It does so in spite of the normal review steps in the Atomic Energy Act of 1954.
plaw-113-229-2014:
Public Law 113-229 is a joint resolution of the 113th Congress that grants honorary United States citizenship. The honor goes to Bernardo de Gaalvez y Madrid, Viscount of Galveston and Count of Gaalvez. The grant notes that the honor had been given only 7 times before. It calls the honor one not lightly given. Gaalvez was a hero of the Revolutionary War who risked his life for the freedom of the United States.

The grant says Gaalvez raised an army of 7,500 men of many lands. His troops took the Port of New Orleans. They beat the British at Baton Rouge, Natchez, and Mobile. His two-month siege of Pensacola took the capital of British West Florida.
plaw-113-230-2014: The short title Corporal Michael J. Crescenz Act of 2013 belongs to Public Law 113-230 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. It names a veterans medical center in Pennsylvania. The Department of Veterans Affairs medical center at 3900 Woodland Avenue in Philadelphia must be known as the Corporal Michael J. Crescenz Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center. Any mention of that center in a federal law, rule, map, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the full name.
plaw-113-231-2014: A veterans clinic in Junction City, Kansas, is named by Public Law 113-231 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The Junction City Community-Based Outpatient Clinic at 715 Southwind Drive becomes the Lieutenant General Richard J. Seitz Community-Based Outpatient Clinic. Findings trace his service. As a Leavenworth High School cadet leader he won the American Legion Cup. At Kansas State he took an Army commission and was called to duty in 1940. He was among the first United States paratroopers. At 25 he led a battalion, the youngest such leader in the Army.
plaw-113-232-2014: Public Law 113-232, the Blackfoot River Land Exchange Act of 2014, swaps land to settle a boundary dispute in Idaho. The 113th Congress passed it for the Fort Hall Indian Reservation. The Blackfoot River had shifted course along the reservation line, which left trust and fee land in dispute. Findings name the Shoshone-Bannock Tribes, a tribe the federal government recognizes. Their base is Fort Hall, Idaho. The tribes adopted a constitution and bylaws on March 31, 1936. The Interior Secretary approved them that April.
plaw-113-233-2014: Ebola's virus family joins a drug review program under Public Law 113-233 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. Its short title is the Adding Ebola to the FDA Priority Review Voucher Program Act. The program rewards work on cures for tropical diseases with faster drug review. Section 524 of the food and drug act gains one item, Filoviruses. Two more edits aid holders of the review vouchers. A voucher may change hands with no cap on transfers. The notice span before use falls from 365 days to 90 days.
plaw-113-234-2014: Galesburg, Illinois, gains a named veterans clinic under Public Law 113-234 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The community based outpatient clinic of the Department of Veterans Affairs stands at 310 Home Boulevard in Galesburg. It must be known as the Lane A. Evans VA Community Based Outpatient Clinic. Any mention of that clinic in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the full name.
plaw-113-235-2014:
Public Law 113-235, the Consolidated and Further Continuing Appropriations Act, 2015, funds the government for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2015. The 113th Congress approved it on December 16, 2014. Early sections cover a statement of the sums, how long funds last, and set sums in place of taxes. One section orders a study of electric rates in the insular areas.

Division A is the farm and food spending act for 2015. Its titles cover farm programs, land saving, and rural growth. They also cover domestic food programs and aid to other lands. The act thus pairs a full-year grant for one division with short-term funds for the rest.
plaw-113-236-2014: Public Law 113-236, the Sudden Unexpected Death Data Enhancement and Awareness Act, targets deaths of the very young. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014 to improve child health and public grasp of such deaths. The Health and Human Services Secretary must keep up work on stillbirth. The same duty covers sudden unexpected infant death and sudden unexplained death in childhood. One task is data work. Facts such as family background, death scene checks, health history, and autopsy results are gathered through systems in place.
plaw-113-237-2014: Title 36 of the United States Code is revised by Public Law 113-237 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. Title 36 covers patriotic and national observances, ceremonies, and groups. Section 2 states the purpose in one line. The act makes the changes needed to keep the title current. It also makes technical fixes and improvements. Section 3 then starts the fixes. The first fix rewrites the title's own table of contents. The sample ends in the middle of that table.
plaw-113-238-2014: Public Law 113-238, the Aviation Security Stakeholder Participation Act of 2014, creates an advisory panel on flight security. The 113th Congress amended title 49 in December 2014. A new section 44946 sets up an Aviation Security Advisory Committee. The panel sits inside the Transportation Security Administration. The head of that office must seek the panel's views as fits. Topics are flight security matters at large. They include how policies, programs, and rules are built and put to work.
plaw-113-239-2014: Public Law 113-239, the Permanent Electronic Duck Stamp Act of 2013, was approved by the 113th Congress in 2014. It gives the Interior Secretary lasting power to let states issue electronic duck stamps. A duck stamp is the federal migratory-bird hunting and conservation stamp of the 1934 Duck Stamp Act. The act calls the paper form the actual stamp. It also defines the state computer systems that issue hunting and fishing licenses, by counter, web, or phone.
plaw-113-240-2014:
Public Law 113-240, the Newborn Screening Saves Lives Reauthorization Act of 2014, renews newborn health programs. The 113th Congress amended part A of title XI of the Public Health Service Act. Section 2 improves screening and follow-up for heritable disorders in newborns and children. Heritable disorders are health faults passed from parent to child.

Later sections judge how well the screening programs work. They cover the advisory panel on such disorders and a clearinghouse of screening facts. They also cover lab quality, a joint panel, and a national backup plan. The Hunter Kelly Research Program and consent for screening research close the list.
plaw-113-241-2014: Two court sites at one San Diego address are named by Public Law 113-241 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The United States Federal Judicial Center at 333 West Broadway becomes the John Rhoades Federal Judicial Center. The center takes in five more sites and a plaza next door. The United States courthouse at the same address becomes the James M. Carter and Judith N. Keep United States Courthouse.
plaw-113-242-2014: Public Law 113-242, the Death in Custody Reporting Act of 2013, presses states to report deaths in custody. The 113th Congress approved it in 2014. A state that takes funds for named programs must report to the Attorney General four times a year. The reports cover the death of any person held, under arrest, or on the way to jail. Jails and prisons in scope span city and county jails and state prisons. State-run and contracted boot camp prisons are named as well.
plaw-113-243-2014: Parts of the FAA Modernization and Reform Act of 2012 are amended by Public Law 113-243 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The topic is rollover of sums received in an airline carrier bankruptcy. Section 1106 set a span to file a claim for refund. The act strikes 2013 and inserts 2015, which adds two years. Term edits follow. One adds a filing date of November 29, 2011. One notes a pension plan frozen as of November 1, 2012.
plaw-113-244-2014: Public Law 113-244, the Crooked River Collaborative Water Security and Jobs Act of 2014, adjusts a river boundary in Oregon. The 113th Congress amended the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act. The Crooked River stretch in scope runs 14.75 miles, from the National Grassland boundary to Dry Creek. A 7-mile part is classed as a recreational river. A 7.75-mile part starts a quarter mile below Bowman Dam and holds the same class. A hydropower part then begins, as the sample breaks off.
plaw-113-245-2014: The Transportation Security Acquisition Reform Act is the name of Public Law 113-245 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. It orders the Transportation Security Administration to use best practice in buying technology. Open books on those programs are a second aim. Findings say the agency has not steadily used Homeland Security policies or government best practice. It built a multiyear technology plan only lately. It has also made poor use of fresh ideas from private firms, small ones included.
plaw-113-246-2014: Public Law 113-246, the Cybersecurity Workforce Assessment Act, orders a review of cyber staff at Homeland Security. The 113th Congress passed it in December 2014. The Secretary must assess the cybersecurity workforce of the Department. A full workforce strategy must follow from that check. Terms sort each post by its main cyber work function and specialty area. The areas come from a national workforce framework report. A 180-day span for the check starts as the sample ends.
plaw-113-247-2014: Prescott, Arizona, gains a named post office under Public Law 113-247 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 442 Miller Valley Road in Prescott must be known as the Barry M. Goldwater Post Office. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name. The act does nothing else.
plaw-113-248-2014: A port land transfer in Iuka, Mississippi, is approved by Public Law 113-248 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The Tennessee Valley Authority Act of 1933 sets the step that Congress must take. Congress approves the Authority's transfer, for the United States, to the State of Mississippi. The land is the Yellow Creek Port properties at Iuka. The United States owns the ground, and the Authority held it as of the day this act passed.
plaw-113-249-2014: An FBI building in Vienna, Virginia, is named by Public Law 113-249 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The building at 801 Follin Lane in Vienna must be known as the Michael D. Resnick Terrorist Screening Center. The name holds only while the Bureau occupies the building. In that span, any mention of the building in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the center name.
plaw-113-250-2014: Small community banks and their towns are aided by Public Law 113-250 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. Its head note speaks of growth, small business, and personal savings. Section 1 orders a rule change by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. Within six months, the Board must publish draft changes to its Small Bank Holding Company Policy Statement. The statement would then cover holding firms with assets below $1,000,000,000. Firms deep in non-bank work are kept out, as the sample starts to state.
plaw-113-251-2014: Public Law 113-251, the American Savings Promotion Act, lets banks offer savings raffle products to spur saving. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014. Findings set the scene. The yearly savings rate in the United States was 4.1 percent in 2012. More than 40 percent of households lack savings to cover three months of basic costs if income stops. Prize-linked savings products work like plain savings accounts. They add chances to win prizes based on deposits made.
plaw-113-252-2014: Public Law 113-252, the Credit Union Share Insurance Fund Parity Act, widens deposit cover at credit unions. The 113th Congress amended the Federal Credit Union Act in 2014. Cover now reaches sums held in a member account for another person. A new part gives pass-through cover for set accounts. The accounts named first are interest on lawyers trust accounts, called IOLTA for short. Like escrow accounts are covered on the same terms, as the new text goes on to state.
plaw-113-253-2014: Lines of some coastal barrier units are revised by Public Law 113-253 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The system in scope is the John H. Chafee Coastal Barrier Resources System. Section 1 replaces three maps for units in North Carolina. They cover the Lea Island Complex, Wrightsville Beach, and Masonboro Island. New maps dated March 12, 2014, take their place. The Interior Secretary must keep the new maps on file for public viewing. A Rhode Island part follows.
plaw-113-254-2014: Chemical site safety rules gain a new home in law under Public Law 113-254 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. It restates and renews the Chemical Facility Anti-Terrorism Standards Program. A new Title XXI in the Homeland Security Act of 2002 holds the program. Early terms name what counts as a CFATS rule. A chemical site of interest is one that holds a chemical of interest. A site the Secretary has fair grounds to think holds one counts as well.
plaw-113-255-2014: Public Law 113-255, the Smart Savings Act, changes the default fund of the Thrift Savings Plan. The 113th Congress amended title 5 in 2014. The Thrift Savings Plan is the retirement savings plan for federal workers. When a saver has made no choice, sums went to a set fund by rule. The new text sends those sums to a target date fund fit for the saver's age. One bar stays for a class of members named in the text. Their sums go to the Government Securities Investment Fund.
plaw-113-256-2014:
The veterans medical center in Waco, Texas, is named by Public Law 113-256 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. It becomes the Doris Miller Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center. Section 1 gives his record. Doris Miller was born in Waco on October 12, 1919. On September 16, 1939, he enlisted in the Navy as a mess attendant, third class, at Dallas.

Miller rose through mess and cook ratings by June 1943. He was carried as missing in action from November 24, 1943. His ship, USS Liscome Bay, was torpedoed and sunk in the Pacific. He won the Navy Cross and the Purple Heart, among other medals.
plaw-113-257-2014: Public Law 113-257, the Veterans Traumatic Brain Injury Care Improvement Act of 2014, extends a pilot program for veterans. The 113th Congress passed it in December 2014. The program gives assisted living services to veterans with traumatic brain injury. It began under a 2008 defense act. Section 2 first rewrites the report rules. For each quarter from January 1, 2015, to September 30, 2017, a report is due. The Veterans Affairs Secretary sends it to the House and Senate veterans panels.
plaw-113-258-2014: A Miami, Arizona, mail site is renamed by Public Law 113-258, approved by the 113th Congress in 2014. The Postal Service site at 161 Live Oak Street must be known as the Staff Sergeant Manuel V. Mendoza Post Office Building. The act is framed as a redesignation, since the site had a name before. References to the site in federal laws, maps, rules, records, and other papers count as references to the new name.
plaw-113-259-2014: Baytown, Texas, gains a named memorial post office under Public Law 113-259 of the 113th Congress, passed in 2014. The site at 601 West Baker Road in Baytown must be known as the Specialist Keith Erin Grace, Jr. Memorial Post Office. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name. The act does nothing else.
plaw-113-260-2014: Public Law 113-260, the Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act of 2014, tightens control of lab-made steroids. The 113th Congress amended the Controlled Substances Act to regulate anabolic steroids with more force. Section 2 adds a long list of named substances to the act's definitions. The names are chemical names for man-made variants of muscle-building drugs. One old list item is renumbered to make room. The sample ends part-way through the added names.
plaw-113-261-2014: Public Law 113-261, passed by the 113th Congress and signed on December 18, 2014, names a stretch of Interstate Route 35 in Minnesota the James L Oberstar Memorial Highway. The named stretch runs from milepost 133 at Forest Lake to milepost 259 at Duluth. The act says that any mention of that stretch in a federal law, map, rule, or record counts as a mention of the new name.
plaw-113-262-2014:
Public Law 113-262, the May 31, 1918 Act Repeal Act, was passed by the 113th Congress in 2014. It deals with the Fort Hall Townsite in Idaho, about 120 acres on the Fort Hall Reservation that an act of May 31, 1918 had taken out of trust. The tribes named in the law are the Shoshone-Bannock Tribes of the Fort Hall Reservation.

The act repeals the 1918 law in full. It then gives the tribes the sole right of first refusal to buy, at fair market value, any townsite land that is offered for sale. Land in the townsite that the tribes or a tribe member own or buy is to be held in trust by the United States for their benefit.
plaw-113-263-2014:
Public Law 113-263, the EPS Service Parts Act of 2014, was passed by the 113th Congress and signed on December 18, 2014. It amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act, the law that sets energy saving rules for many products. The subject here is external power supplies, the small adapters that charge or run many devices.

The act carves out a limited break from a February 10, 2014 federal efficiency rule. A power supply can skip that rule if it was made between February 10, 2016 and February 10, 2020, carries the right efficiency mark, and meets the older Level IV standard. It must also be sold as a service part or spare part for a product already in use.
plaw-113-264-2014:
Hunters who pursue migratory birds buy a federal stamp, and Public Law 113-264, the Federal Duck Stamp Act of 2014, raised its price. The 113th Congress passed the law in 2014, amending the Migratory Bird Hunting and Conservation Stamp Act. The added money is meant to pay for conservation easements that protect land for migratory birds.

The act sets the stamp price at 25 dollars for each hunting year after 2013. It also lets the Secretary lower the price for a year if the higher price cut the total money raised. Amounts above 15 dollars from each stamp go into a set subaccount in the conservation fund.
plaw-113-265-2014:
Public Law 113-265, the EARLY Act Reauthorization of 2014, was passed by the 113th Congress and signed on December 18, 2014. EARLY stands for the Young Women's Breast Health Education and Awareness Requires Learning Young Act of 2009. That earlier law set up federal work to teach young women about breast cancer and breast health.

The 2014 act keeps the program going by changing the funding line in the Public Health Service Act. It replaces the old amount with 4,900,000 dollars for each of the fiscal years 2015 through 2019. It also orders a report, due within two years, listing federal breast cancer education work and flagging any efforts that repeat each other.
plaw-113-266-2014: In California, the post office at 73839 Gorgonio Drive in Twentynine Palms takes a new name under Public Law 113-266. It becomes the Colonel M J Mac Dube, USMC Post Office Building. The 113th Congress passed the naming act in 2014. Federal laws, maps, rules, and records must use that name for the site from then on.
plaw-113-267-2014: One post office in Lompoc, California is renamed by Public Law 113-267, an act of the 113th Congress from 2014. The site at 801 West Ocean Avenue becomes the Federal Correctional Officer Scott J Williams Memorial Post Office Building. The new name binds in every federal record that mentions the site. The act has two parts: the naming itself, and a rule for how later references to the site are read.
plaw-113-268-2014: Public Law 113-268 gives a new name to the post office at 101 East Market Street in Long Beach, California: the Juanita Millender-McDonald Post Office. Congress passed the act in 2014. From then on, federal records refer to the site by that name. Two sections make up the whole act, one for the naming and one for later references.
plaw-113-269-2014:
Public Law 113-269, the Propane Education and Research Enhancement Act of 2014, makes two small changes to the law that governs the Propane Education and Research Council. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014. The council is the propane industry body charged with safety, training, and research work under the Propane Education and Research Act of 1996.

First, the act adds a task to the council's list of jobs: training propane sellers and users in ways to soften the harm of future propane price spikes. Second, it changes the price data used in the council's market survey and consumer price study. The study now uses the refiner price to end users of consumer grade propane, as published by the Energy Information Administration.
plaw-113-270-2014:
Public Law 113-270 carries a blunt name: the No Social Security for Nazis Act. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014, and it amends the Social Security Act. Its findings say Congress built Social Security to pay earned benefits to workers and their families. Congress never meant people who took part in Nazi persecution to live in the United States or draw those benefits.

The act cuts off benefits by tying them to removal and loss of citizenship. A person with a final removal order based on taking part in Nazi persecution counts as removed as of the date that order became final. The same holds for a person whose grant of citizenship was taken back for that conduct, or for hiding or lying about it.
plaw-113-271-2014: Public Law 113-271 does one narrow thing: it keeps the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom alive for one more year. Passed by the 113th Congress in 2014, it amends the International Religious Freedom Act of 1998. It swaps 2015 for 2014 in the funding line and moves the end date from September 30, 2014 to September 30, 2015. The changes count as if passed on December 10, 2014.
plaw-113-272-2014:
After Russia moved against Ukraine, Congress answered with Public Law 113-272, the Ukraine Freedom Support Act of 2014. The 113th Congress passed the law in 2014. Its stated aims are to place sanctions on the Russian Federation and to give Ukraine more aid.

The act's sections set up sanctions tied to Russia's defense and energy sectors, plus sanctions on Russian and other foreign banks. Other sections raise military aid for the government of Ukraine and expand aid that is not military. The law also expands broadcasting in countries of the former Soviet Union, backs Russian democracy and civil society groups, and calls for a report on Russia breaking the INF Treaty.
plaw-113-273-2014:
Cleaning up the Chesapeake Bay takes work from many federal programs, and Public Law 113-273 tries to make that spending easy to track. The Chesapeake Bay Accountability and Recovery Act of 2014 was passed by the 113th Congress. It covers the bay watershed, meaning all streams, backwaters, and side channels that drain into the bay, across Maryland, West Virginia, Delaware, New York, Virginia, Pennsylvania, and the District of Columbia.

The act orders the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to prepare a crosscut budget for restoration work in the watershed. A crosscut budget pulls the spending of many agencies into one view. The law first defines its key terms, including what counts as a federal restoration activity and who the state chief executives are.
plaw-113-274-2014:
Public Law 113-274, the Cybersecurity Enhancement Act of 2014, sets up a voluntary team-up between government and private firms to improve computer security. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014. The law states up front that it grants no new power to regulate and allows no new funds.

Its titles cover four areas. The first covers public-private teamwork on computer security. The second covers federal research, including work at the National Institute of Standards and Technology and security checklists for government systems. The third covers training and jobs, with contests and a scholarship-for-service program. The fourth covers public awareness and readiness, so people and firms are better set for attacks.
plaw-113-275-2014: Public Law 113-275 is a single sentence long. Passed by the 113th Congress and signed on December 18, 2014, it amends the Violence Against Women Reauthorization Act of 2013. The act repeals section 910 of that 2013 law, which was a special rule for the State of Alaska. Nothing else in the earlier law is changed by this text.
plaw-113-276-2014:
Surplus United States Navy ships go to other countries under Public Law 113-276, passed by the 113th Congress in 2014. Its first title is the Naval Vessel Transfer Act of 2013. The ships named are Oliver Hazard Perry class guided missile frigates, a class the Navy was retiring.

The act lets the President give two frigates to Mexico as a grant: the USS Curts and the USS McClusky. Four more frigates, the USS Taylor, Gary, Carr, and Elrod, may be sold to the Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office, the Taiwan body named under the Taiwan Relations Act. The President may also swap which named ship goes to which named country, under the same terms.
plaw-113-277-2014:
Public Law 113-277, the Border Patrol Agent Pay Reform Act of 2014, rewrites how border patrol agents are paid for hours past a normal workweek. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014, amending title 5 of the United States Code. Its stated aims are to keep agents ready to do needed work and to give their agency room to cover shift changes and assign work as needs change.

The act adds a new pay section with set rates. A level 1 rate pays 1.25 times the agent's normal hourly pay, and a level 2 rate pays 1.125 times that pay. The text defines who counts as a border patrol agent by job series, and it ties the higher rates to work beyond a 40-hour week.
plaw-113-278-2014:
Public Law 113-278, the Venezuela Defense of Human Rights and Civil Society Act of 2014, was passed by the 113th Congress. It aims to place targeted sanctions on people blamed for abusing the rights of antigovernment protesters in Venezuela, and to strengthen civil society there.

The act opens with long findings about Venezuela's state in 2013 and 2014. It cites an inflation rate of 56.3 percent in 2013, a scarcity index of 29.4 percent in March 2014, and a murder rate of 79 per 100,000 people in 2013. It also quotes Human Rights Watch on power gathered in the executive branch and on critics being censored and prosecuted.
plaw-113-279-2014:
Public Law 113-279, the Insurance Capital Standards Clarification Act of 2014, clears up how one part of the Dodd-Frank Act applies to insurers. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014. Section 171 of the Dodd-Frank Act sets leverage and risk-based capital rules, and firms in the insurance business had faced doubt about how those bank-style rules fit them.

The act adds plain definitions to section 171. It defines the business of insurance, a person regulated by a state insurance regulator, and regulated foreign units of insurers. A foreign unit counts only when it acts as a regulated insurance body. The Federal Reserve Board can still rule that the foreign capital rules in a given case do not meet the law's test.
plaw-113-280-2014:
Public Law 113-280 keeps the United States Anti-Doping Agency in place. The United States Anti-Doping Agency Reauthorization Act was passed by the 113th Congress in 2014. It amends title VII of the Office of National Drug Control Policy Reauthorization Act of 2006, the part of law that defines the agency's role in sport.

The changes update the agency's duties in the words of the law. It is to be known worldwide as the nation's own anti-doping body, apart from government control. Its work covers banned drugs and banned performance methods that the agency itself adopts, a shift from older text that named gene-doping in each clause. The act then rewrites the funding line for the agency.
plaw-113-281-2014:
Coast Guard funding for fiscal year 2015 is the core of Public Law 113-281, the Howard Coble Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Act of 2014. The 113th Congress passed the law in 2014. Title I allows spending for the service and sets the allowed levels of military strength and training.

Title II works through Coast Guard rules in detail. Its sections cover officers and the Commandant, prevention and response crews, centers of skill, penalties, and agreements. Other sections deal with tuition help that covers textbooks, housing, leases, family support and child care, and a yearly Board of Visitors. The act is named for Howard Coble, and its scope is the running of the service for that year.
plaw-113-282-2014:
Public Law 113-282, the National Cybersecurity Protection Act of 2014, puts an existing operations center for computer security into law. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014. The center is the national cybersecurity and communications integration center, which sits inside the Department of Homeland Security.

The act adds a new section 226 to the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to set the center up in statute. It first defines its terms, including cybersecurity risk, critical infrastructure, and information sharing and analysis organizations. Naming the center in law gives the hub, which joins federal and private security work, a firm legal base rather than one based only on agency practice.
plaw-113-283-2014:
Federal agencies guard huge stores of data, and Public Law 113-283, the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014, reforms the rules for that work. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014. It amends chapter 35 of title 44 of the United States Code, the part long known as FISMA.

The act strikes the old subchapters and writes a new information security subchapter. Its stated aims are to give a full framework for security controls and to keep minimum controls in place. It also runs oversight across the civilian, national security, and law enforcement parts of government. It also backs machine tools that test security without pause, and notes that products built by private firms offer strong, up-to-date protection.
plaw-113-284-2014:
Public Law 113-284, the DHS OIG Mandates Revision Act of 2014, cuts required reports from the work list of the Department of Homeland Security Office of Inspector General. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014. The office is the department's own watchdog, and older laws had piled set duties on it over the years.

The act repeals three standing duties. Gone is the yearly check of the cargo inspection targeting system under a 2004 Coast Guard law. Gone is the yearly review of Coast Guard performance under the Homeland Security Act. Gone too is a set part of the yearly review of grants to states and high-risk urban areas. Each repeal comes with small fixes that renumber the text left behind.
plaw-113-285-2014:
One small city airport is freed from federal limits by Public Law 113-285, passed by the 113th Congress in 2014. The law tells the United States to release the City of St Clair, Missouri, from all limits on the use, pledging, sale, and closure of the St Clair Regional Airport. The release runs through the head of the Federal Aviation Administration.

The release comes with terms the city must meet first. The city or its chosen party must hand the Missouri Department of Transportation money for airport capital work, plus all city-owned airport gear the state finds worth saving, for no payment. The money owed is tied to the fair market value of the airport land at its best use, as set by a skilled outside appraiser, plus grant sums the text spells out.
plaw-113-286-2014: Public Law 113-286, the Foreclosure Relief and Extension for Servicemembers Act of 2014, moves two dates and nothing more. Passed by the 113th Congress, it amends a 2012 veterans law that had lengthened the shield guarding service members from mortgage foreclosure and eviction. The end date moves from December 31, 2014 to December 31, 2015, and a linked date moves from January 1, 2015 to January 1, 2016.
plaw-113-287-2014:
Laws about the national parks were gathered into one new title of the United States Code by Public Law 113-287, passed by the 113th Congress and signed on December 19, 2014. The act enacts title 54, named National Park Service and Related Programs, as positive law. Positive law means the code text itself is the law, not just proof of it.

The stated aim is to codify the laws on the National Park System while keeping the intent Congress had when it first passed them. The work strips out unclear points, clashes, and flaws. Along with the new title, the act carries matching fixes to other laws, cross-reference updates, bridge and savings rules, and repeals of the old text it replaces.
plaw-113-288-2014:
Coin collectors get stronger tools against fakes under Public Law 113-288, the Collectible Coin Protection Act. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014, amending the Hobby Protection Act. That older law bars making or selling imitation coins and other hobby items in ways that fool buyers.

The act makes it a breach to give real help or backing to a maker, importer, or seller whom the helper knows, or should have known, is breaking the act. It also bars the sale of such items in commerce, not just their spread. Where a breach also uses the marks of a coin grading service without leave, the mark's owner gains the full rights given by the Trademark Act of 1946.
plaw-113-289-2014:
Safe water for the world's poorest people is the aim of Public Law 113-289, the Senator Paul Simon Water for the World Act of 2014. The 113th Congress passed it to strengthen a 2005 act of the same family. Its sense of Congress says water and sanitation shape many parts of human life, and the United States should lead in helping the most at-risk people gain lasting access to both.

The act sharpens how the government runs its water work. It adds hygiene to the safe water and sanitation aid written into the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961. Later sections, named in the text, work on joining up and watching water, sanitation, and hygiene projects. In that way the government can build skill, use its funds with more force, and judge results with care.
plaw-113-290-2014: A one-line fix is all of Public Law 113-290, the Grand Portage Band Per Capita Adjustment Act, passed by the 113th Congress in 2014. It amends an act of October 19, 1973 about taxable income paid to members of the Grand Portage Band of Lake Superior Chippewa Indians. The change adds the Grand Portage Band by name to a clause on equal treatment of set per capita income when federal aid is counted. The clause ties the payments to the agreements of each band.
plaw-113-291-2014:
Public Law 113-291 is the yearly defense policy law: the Carl Levin and Howard P Buck McKeon National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2015. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014. Its stated job is to allow spending for fiscal year 2015 on military work of the Department of Defense, on military building, and on defense work of the Department of Energy. It also sets military staffing levels for that year.

The act opens with findings in honor of its namesakes. They trace Senator Carl Levin's path from Detroit schools to Harvard Law School, his city council years, and his long run on the Senate Armed Services Committee, which he joined in 1979. The findings note the committee had passed a defense law each year for 52 years.
plaw-113-292-2014: The Postal Service site at 18640 NW 2nd Avenue in Miami, Florida becomes the Father Richard Marquess-Barry Post Office Building under Public Law 113-292. The 113th Congress passed the naming act in 2014. Any federal mention of the site counts as a mention of the new name. Nothing else changes: the act pairs the naming with a short rule on references.
plaw-113-293-2014:
Spy agencies run on money Congress allows in laws like Public Law 113-293, the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2015. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014. It allows spending for fiscal years 2014 and 2015 on intelligence work of the United States Government, the Community Management Account, and the Central Intelligence Agency Retirement and Disability System.

Title I covers intelligence work itself, with a classified schedule of allowed sums and rules for staff caps. Title II funds the CIA retirement system. Title III holds general rules. Among them are a rise in worker pay and benefits allowed by law, a bar on carrying out intelligence work outside the law's terms, a national intelligence strategy, and software licensing.
plaw-113-294-2014: Public Law 113-294 caps the security fee charged to airline passengers. Passed by the 113th Congress in 2014, it amends title 49 of the United States Code. The fee is set at 5 dollars and 60 cents for a one-way trip that starts at an airport in the United States. No more than 11 dollars and 20 cents may be charged for a round trip. The cap binds trips bought on or after the day the act passed.
plaw-113-295-2014:
Public Law 113-295 is a year-end tax law in two parts, passed by the 113th Congress in 2014. Division A is the Tax Increase Prevention Act of 2014, which extends tax rules that were about to lapse and makes fixes to the Internal Revenue Code of 1986. Division B, named in the act's own heading, sets the tax treatment of ABLE accounts, state-run savings accounts for the care of family members with disabilities.

The table of contents shows the reach of Division A. One title extends breaks for single taxpayers, such as the write-off for costs borne by grade school teachers and the bar on taxing forgiven home loan debt. More titles follow for business and energy breaks, each saving a named rule from its end date.
plaw-113-296-2014:
Public Law 113-296, the United States-Israel Strategic Partnership Act of 2014, sets out to deepen ties between the two countries. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014. Its findings speak of a deep and unbreakable bond built over more than 60 years of shared interests and shared values. They also speak of a fast-changing security scene in the Middle East and North Africa.

The findings name the threats Congress saw: Hamas firing rockets from Gaza, Hezbollah storing rockets with help from Iran, and Iran seeking nuclear weapons. The policy section then states the stance of the United States. It backs the security of Israel as a Jewish state without wavering. It also restates the aims of the United States-Israel Enhanced Security Cooperation Act of 2012, calling for that law to be carried out in full.
plaw-113-73-2014: Public Law 113-73 is a three-day bridge. Passed by the 113th Congress on January 15, 2014, this joint resolution makes further continuing appropriations for fiscal year 2014. Its whole operative text amends the Continuing Appropriations Act, 2014: the end date named in section 106(3) of that act is struck, and January 18, 2014 takes its place. The swap kept the government funded while a full-year law was finished.
plaw-113-74-2014: Public Law 113-74, the Accuracy for Adoptees Act, tells federal offices to trust state court papers on one point. Passed by the 113th Congress in 2014, it amends section 320 of the Immigration and Nationality Act. A Certificate of Citizenship or other federal paper must show a child's name and date of birth as given on a state court order or birth record. A like state record from the child's home state counts as well, once the child has been adopted or readopted in that state.
plaw-113-75-2014: Two NASA sites in California trade names under Public Law 113-75, passed by the 113th Congress in 2014. The Hugh L Dryden Flight Research Center at Edwards becomes the NASA Neil A Armstrong Flight Research Center. The Western Aeronautical Test Range becomes the NASA Hugh L Dryden Aeronautical Test Range, so the Dryden name moves to the range. Any mention of either site in a federal law, map, rule, or record counts as a mention of its new name.
plaw-113-76-2014:
Public Law 113-76, the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2014, is the full-year funding law for fiscal year 2014. The 113th Congress passed it in January 2014. It makes consolidated appropriations for the year ending September 30, 2014, paying for nearly the whole federal government in one act.

The front of the act sets shared rules on references, the explanatory statement, fund use, and a launch liability extension. The act then runs as a stack of divisions. Division A funds agriculture, rural growth, the Food and Drug Administration, and kin agencies, with titles for farm programs, conservation, rural growth, and food aid at home and abroad. Division B funds commerce, justice, science, and kin agencies, with titles for the Commerce and Justice Departments, science, and related agencies.
plaw-113-77-2014:
Public Law 113-77, the Poison Center Network Act, renews the system that answers calls when a child swallows something harmful. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014, amending the Public Health Service Act. It reauthorizes three linked parts: the poison center national toll-free number, a national media campaign, and a grant program for centers.

Section 2 funds the phone line, allowing 700,000 dollars for each of the fiscal years 2015 through 2019 to keep the nationwide toll-free number running. Section 3 funds the media push that urges people to use the centers, at 800,000 dollars a year over the same span. Section 4 renews the grant program, swapping the word accredited for certified in the program's terms.
plaw-113-78-2014:
A memorial to the Peace Corps gets the go-ahead in Public Law 113-78, passed by the 113th Congress in 2014. The act lets the Peace Corps Commemorative Foundation set up a commemorative work on federal land in the District of Columbia and its area. The work is to honor the mission of the Peace Corps and the ideals on which it was founded.

The build must follow the Commemorative Works Act, the law in chapter 89 of title 40. No federal funds may pay any cost of the work. The foundation alone takes gifts for it and pays its costs. If money is left once all costs and the upkeep sum are paid, the rest goes to the Secretary of the Interior for the account that law names. The same holds once the time to build runs out.
plaw-113-79-2014:
Public Law 113-79 is the farm bill: the Agricultural Act of 2014. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014 to reform and carry on the farm and food programs of the Department of Agriculture through fiscal year 2018. Its first title covers commodities, the crops that get federal price and income support.

Subtitle A of Title I repeals three older tools: direct payments, counter-cyclical payments, and the average crop revenue election program. A new commodity policy then takes their place, built on base acres, payment yields, and a producer election. The named tools are price loss coverage and agriculture risk coverage, with transition aid for upland cotton growers. Subtitle B opens with marketing loans for crops.
plaw-113-80-2014:
Public Law 113-80, the OPM IG Act, gives a watchdog its own funding stream. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014, amending title 5 of the United States Code. The Office of Personnel Management runs a revolving fund, a pot of money refilled by the work it pays for, and its Inspector General is the office's internal watchdog.

The act says fund money may pay the cost of audits, probes, and oversight work the Inspector General runs on the fund and on the work the fund pays for. The office budget must carry the Inspector General's own estimate of the sum needed for that work. That request may not top 0.33 percent of the total budget authority the office seeks.
plaw-113-81-2014:
Public Law 113-81, the Support for United States-Republic of Korea Civil Nuclear Cooperation Act, buys time for an atomic energy pact. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014 to let the President stretch the term of the nuclear energy agreement with the Republic of Korea until March 19, 2016. The pact in force was due to lapse on March 19, 2014, while a new one was still being negotiated.

The findings frame the deal. In the 60th year of the alliance, ties between the two countries could not be stronger, the act says, resting on shared sacrifice, respect, and interests. It names North Korea's nuclear weapons work, uranium enrichment and plutonium reprocessing among them, as a threat to the Korean Peninsula. Both countries back the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons and share trade and safety stakes in their peaceful nuclear programs.
plaw-113-82-2014:
Military retirees under 62 were due a smaller yearly raise under a 2013 budget deal, and Public Law 113-82 takes that cut off the table for those in uniform. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014. Its heading states the aim in full. The reduced cost-of-living adjustment required by the Bipartisan Budget Act of 2013 will not apply to members or former members who first became members before January 1, 2014.

The act adds a coverage clause to section 1401a of title 10. The reduced raise applies to a member or former member who first joined a uniformed service on or after January 1, 2014. The change takes effect on December 1, 2015. A first section pays for the shift by extending a direct spending reduction into fiscal year 2024. A later section reworks a fund for reform of the doctor pay growth rate in the Social Security Act.
plaw-113-83-2014:
Public Law 113-83, the Temporary Debt Limit Extension Act, lifts the federal debt cap for just over a year. The 113th Congress passed it in February 2014. Section 3101(b) of title 31, the clause that caps total federal debt, is set aside from the day the act passes through March 15, 2015.

On March 16, 2015 the cap snaps back, raised by the amount of new debt issued in the window that tops the sum owed on the day the act passed. A debt counts only if it was needed to pay a bill the government owed by law before that date. The act also bars the Secretary of the Treasury from issuing debt in the window just to build up a cash pile past normal levels ahead of the deadline.
plaw-113-84-2014: Public Law 113-84 is a joint resolution that fills one seat. Passed by the 113th Congress in 2014, it appoints John Fahey of the District of Columbia as a citizen regent of the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution. He takes the seat left open when the term of Roger W Sant of the District of Columbia ended on October 24, 2013. The appointment runs for six years from the day the resolution passes, under section 5581 of the Revised Statutes.
plaw-113-85-2014: Public Law 113-85 is a joint resolution that fills one seat. Passed by the 113th Congress in 2014, it appoints Risa Lavizzo-Mourey of Pennsylvania as a citizen regent of the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution. She fills the gap left when the term of Patricia Q Stonesifer of Washington, DC ended on December 21, 2013. The six-year term starts on the later of December 22, 2013 or the day the resolution passed, under section 5581 of the Revised Statutes.
plaw-113-86-2014:
Public Law 113-86, the National Integrated Drought Information System Reauthorization Act of 2014, renews the federal drought watch system. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014, amending the National Integrated Drought Information System Act of 2006. A new clause states the aim in plain terms: to better inform and allow faster choices that cut the harm and cost of drought.

The act rewrites the system's duties. It must run a strong early warning system that gathers and joins data on the key signs of drought and its impacts. The system turns that data into usable, sound forecasts on time, at both national and regional levels. It must share those forecasts, conditions, and impacts on an ongoing basis with planners at every level of government, with private firms, and with the public. Its data and products must reflect how drought differs from place to place.
plaw-113-87-2014:
Public Law 113-87, the Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore Conservation and Recreation Act, sets aside wilderness along Lake Michigan in Michigan. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014. Under the Wilderness Act, set land and inland water inside the Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore are named as wilderness and as part of the National Wilderness Preservation System.

The new Sleeping Bear Dunes Wilderness takes in about 32,557 acres along the mainland shore and on nearby islands in Benzie and Leelanau Counties. Its lines are drawn on a six-sheet map from November 2010. The Secretary of the Interior must keep the map on file for public viewing and may fix clerical or typing slips in it. The Secretary must also draw up a legal account of the line and send it to the Senate energy panel named in the text.
plaw-113-88-2014: Public Law 113-88 frees one tribe's own land from a federal consent rule. Passed by the 113th Congress in 2014, it lets the Fond du Lac Band of Lake Superior Chippewa in Minnesota deal in its own land. The band may lease, sell, convey, warrant, or hand over any part of its stake in real property that is not held in trust by the United States. No further federal say-so is needed. The act does not touch trust land, and federal law on trust land transfers stands as it was.
plaw-113-89-2014:
Flood insurance bills spiked after a 2012 reform, and Public Law 113-89, the Homeowner Flood Insurance Affordability Act of 2014, slows the rise. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014. Its heading says it delays the start of set parts of the Biggert-Waters Flood Insurance Reform Act of 2012.

The contents list shows the tools. One section repeals set rate rises outright, and the next restores grandfathered rates. Others set rules for yearly rate rises, clear up rates for homes newly mapped into high-risk flood zones, and add a yearly premium surcharge. More clauses allow monthly premium payments, high-deductible plans for homes, and an exemption for detached buildings from the must-buy rule, plus funds to repay homeowners who win map appeals.
plaw-113-90-2014: Public Law 113-90, the Home Heating Emergency Assistance Through Transportation Act of 2014, is called the HHEATT Act for short. Passed by the 113th Congress, it tackles shortages of propane and other home heating fuels. An emergency exemption from trucking rules, issued by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration for haulers aiding propane and heating fuel delivery, stays in force until May 31, 2014. The Secretary of Transportation may end it sooner if, after checking with the governors of the hit states, the crisis is over.
plaw-113-91-2014: Public Law 113-91 is a joint resolution that keeps one regent in his seat. Passed by the 113th Congress in 2014, it reappoints John W McCarter of Illinois as a citizen regent of the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution. His earlier term ended on March 14, 2014. The new six-year term starts on March 15, 2014, or on the day the resolution passed if that is later, under section 5581 of the Revised Statutes.
plaw-113-92-2014:
Public Law 113-92, the Philippines Charitable Giving Assistance Act, speeds up the tax break for gifts that aid victims of Typhoon Haiyan in the Philippines. The 113th Congress passed it in March 2014, weeks after the storm. It works through section 170 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, the clause that allows a tax write-off for charity gifts.

A taxpayer may treat a covered cash gift made after the act passed and before April 15, 2014 as if it were made on December 31, 2013. That shift puts the write-off a year sooner. A gift counts if it is cash, given for the relief of victims in areas hit by the typhoon, and fit for the write-off under section 170. A phone bill that shows the charity's name, the date, and the sum counts as proof of the gift.
plaw-113-93-2014:
Public Law 113-93, the Protecting Access to Medicare Act of 2014, is a yearly patch for doctor pay and a bundle of health programs. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014, amending the Social Security Act. Its heading says it extends Medicare payments to physicians and other parts of the Medicare and Medicaid programs.

Title I is named Medicare Extenders. Its first section gives a physician payment update. The rest stretch set rules past their end dates: a floor for the work cost index, the therapy cap exceptions process, and ambulance add-on payments. Higher hospital payments for low-volume hospitals are on the list too. The list runs on to the Medicare-dependent hospital program, special Medicare Advantage plans for people with special needs, and reasonable cost contracts.
plaw-113-94-2014:
Public Law 113-94, the Gabriella Miller Kids First Research Act, takes money once used for party conventions and aims it at children's health research. The 113th Congress passed it in 2014. It ends taxpayer financing of political party conventions and shifts the savings to a ten-year pediatric research initiative run through the Common Fund of the National Institutes of Health.

The act amends section 9008 of the tax code. From the day the act passes, the right of any major or minor party to a payment under that section ends. All sums in each party account move to a new Treasury pot, the 10-Year Pediatric Research Initiative Fund. That money may be spent only for the pediatric research ends named in the Public Health Service Act, and only as far as funding laws allow in advance.
plaw-113-95-2014:
Public Law 113-95 carries a long name: the Support for the Sovereignty, Integrity, Democracy, and Economic Stability of Ukraine Act of 2014. The 113th Congress passed it in April 2014, as Ukraine faced pressure from Russia. Its one-line heading states the core aim: to provide for the costs of loan guarantees for Ukraine.

The text in hand is the start of the act, and it is built from definitions. It names the congressional panels that count as the right ones to deal with, spanning foreign affairs, intelligence, and appropriations in both houses, plus party leaders. It defines a United States person and the term materially assisted, which it ties to the acts spelled out in sections 8 and 9 of the law.
plaw-113-96-2014:
Public Law 113-96 turns to the airwaves in a fight over Ukraine. Its title is United States International Programming to Ukraine and Neighboring Regions, and the 113th Congress passed it in April 2014. Congress finds that the Russian Government has blocked the Ukrainian people's access to uncensored news and fed them news that is wrong and inflammatory in its place.
